note: No automated with-skill/baseline test runs were executed for this skill, for the same reasons documented in the sibling nafezly-apply skill's evals.json: (1) the workflow's only real effect - submitting a live offer to a real client on mostaql.com - spends real credibility and a literal, capped monthly bid quota, so it shouldn't be triggered repeatedly as a 'test'; (2) the skill drives the same single shared Chrome profile as nafezly-apply, so parallel with-skill/baseline subagent runs aren't mechanically possible. The skill's logic is a direct distillation of a live research pass completed in the same session it was authored in (2026-08-30): logged into mostaql.com via the shared browser, browsed the development project category, opened several real project-detail pages (including a senior infra/DevOps role with a hard filter test - 'any generic or copy-paste offer gets ignored' plus three numbered required-answer questions - and an MVP build asking for a PHP/Python stack outside the target skillset), and read the real offer-submission form end to end. No bid was placed during that research pass; the strongest candidate found (the senior infra/DevOps project) was flagged to the user as a borderline-fit option worth a deliberate look rather than bid on reflexively. Treat the user's first live invocation of this skill as iteration 1's real-world test; revise based on what actually happens then, per the skill-creator iteration loop.

evals.expected_output: Skill checks browser access and remaining bid quota, browses the development category on mostaql.com, applies the filter checklist (including the quota-aware bar) to open projects, submits real offers only to genuine matches (or reports zero if none clear the bar), and ends with a plain-language summary including remaining quota.
